about.title: ECHO/trace
about.tagline: Authoritarian propaganda does not invent new language. It inherits it.
about.lead: ECHO/trace is an autonomous pattern-matching system that exposes this inheritance in real time. Every six hours, it scrapes 30+ state media outlets across authoritarian regimes, identifies rhetorical patterns using a 22-trope taxonomy, and matches them against a historical archive of 20th-century dictatorships.
about.output: The output: forensic pairings that juxtapose today's propaganda with its structural ancestors — a Putin spokesman echoing Goebbels, Chinese state media recycling Stalin, Iranian broadcasts mirroring Mussolini.
about.mechanism: The system operates as a digital archaeologist, analyzing each article across 18 scientific dimensions drawn from propaganda studies, semiotics, and genocide prevention research. It searches for structural DNA matches in archives from Nazi Germany, Stalinist USSR, Maoist China, and Fascist Italy — the most thoroughly documented propaganda corpora in history.
about.clinical: The analysis is clinical; the conclusions are implicit in the parallelism.
about.parallel: Just parallel quotes, timestamped and traced.
about.closing: Making inheritance visible is the point.
